elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 13.5 still deems the Termination for Convenience Fee to be "liquidated damages and not a penalty," and Section 11.1 still obliges Customer to pay that fee (capped at three months' fees). A Customer-payable liquidated amount therefore survives, so the preferred level is not reached (as the drafter concedes in the comment).

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2(A) no longer imposes a Termination for Cause Fee ("Customer shall not be liable for any termination fee or other liquidated amount"), and Section 13.5 now references only the Section 11.1 Termination for Convenience Fee — expressly an "early termination fee." The other retained Customer payments (unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses of disposition) are actual-cost reimbursements, not liquidated amounts.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 as rendered: early termination fee "in an amount not to exceed three (3) months of fees payable by Customer under this Agreement," replacing the REDACTED percentage of Estimated Remaining Value (remaining months x monthly fees). The cap is at, not above, the fallback threshold.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 13.5 as rendered states the Termination for Convenience Fee "is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement," and the competing Cause Fee has been removed from both 11.2(A) and 13.5, so the statement is internally consistent.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: single Customer-payable liquidated amount, expressly an early-termination fee, capped at exactly three months' fees, and declared the sole liquidated amount; no element is left to the margin comment.

Preferred level fails only because the capped Termination for Convenience Fee is still characterised as liquidated damages in Section 13.5 — to reach preferred the drafter would have to delete the fee obligation in 11.1 and Section 13.5 entirely.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to the fee's quantum (11.1), the duplicate Cause Fee (11.2(A)), and the conforming recital (13.5). Favourable and unrelated retained language survives untouched — the one-year notice right, the 50/50 payment mechanics, the Conversion/Expenses reimbursement, the 11.1 carve-out from Section 13.4, and the now-unused "Estimated Remaining Value" definition (correctly left in place rather than deleted, since a defined term may be used elsewhere and an unused definition creates no dangling reference).

Note for the drafter: the substitute wording in 11.2(A) ("shall not be liable for any termination fee or other liquidated amount") is marginally broader than the checklist requires, since the checklist only regulates liquidated amounts. It remains defensible because the deleted Cause Fee was itself designated liquidated damages in 13.5, but a plain deletion of the Cause Fee sentence would be the tightest form if Vendor pushes back on the added prohibition.

Intent preserved: deleting the Cause Fee correctly carried with it the dependent sentence disapplying Section 13.4 (which would otherwise reference a non-existent fee), and 13.5's cross-reference to "Sections 11.1 or 11.2(A)" was conformed to "Section 11.1," leaving no dangling reference or contradictory retained sentence.

Walk-away exposure is cured: the fee is no longer measured by remaining contract value, and the minor-breach trigger (failure to give the 11.1 notice, or any Customer Event of Default) no longer carries a liquidated payment.
